covers: 1. relative-target nominal command direction and magnitude
2. zero-distance command (hover, not random)
3. speed saturation far away (capped at max_speed)
4. low-speed command near asset (proportional scaling at 12/6/3/2/1 m)
5. hover command via the controller (filter_velocity identity on zero input)
6. acceleration limiting (single substep from rest, capped at a_max*dt_sub)
7. horizontal-speed limiting (command far beyond 12 m/s capped)
8. climb limiting (command far beyond 5 m/s climb capped)
9. descent limiting (command far beyond 5 m/s descent capped)
10. velocity reversal with no legacy heading/turn-rate limit (passes through near-zero speed, no forced curve)
11. 0.1s substep count (5 per 0.5s) and misconfigured-dt rejection
12. deterministic execution (two independent envs, same seed, identical trajectory)
13. identity safety-filter behavior (v_safe == v_nom bit-for-bit, zero constraints)
14. diagnostic fields present/correct in cbf_velocity mode, and neutral defaults in legacy mode
15. no-defender test configuration (intercept_radius=1e-6; no interception outcomes over 20 episodes)
16. common-random-number asset trajectory across control modes (identical soldier_pos every step)
17. canonical endurance budget (= path_factor * initial 3-D distance)
18. swept capture detected under substepped motion (captures terminate within the 2 m radius)
19. bit-for-bit legacy A0 no-op vs the parent commit (git-show-based dynamic module comparison, 30 seeds)
gate boundary cases; namespace disjointness + protocol stability; constraint verification on a 30-episode sample
note: the full 1,000-episode foundation validation and 1,000-seed legacy no-op check are run by experiments/journal_cbf_attacker_run.py (restart-safe, chunked) and recorded under docs/journal_cbf_attacker/foundation/; this suite uses smaller seed counts for CI speed.
